title: The ‘Manosphere’ Isn’t a Movement. It’s a Multibillion-Dollar Grievance Industry
gist: A 153-page Reset Tech / Equimundo report reframes the online 'manosphere' as a multibillion-dollar consumer funnel rather than a political movement: aspirational self-help content routes young men into paid communities, unregulated supplements, crypto schemes and high-ticket coaching, with Andrew Tate's $99/month 'Real World' alone estimated at $184 million in annual gross revenue. The study argues the reach behind it is manufactured by recommendation algorithms (14.6 billion views across 216 looksmaxxing influencers), and that platforms have never applied to male body-image content the enforcement they eventually applied to pro-eating-disorder content aimed at women.

insights.claim: A Reset Tech and Equimundo report argues the online 'manosphere' is better modeled as a commercial pyramid scheme than as an organic right-wing political movement, with young men algorithmically routed into paid communities, unregulated supplements, crypto schemes and high-ticket coaching programs.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Reclassifies a culture-war phenomenon as a consumer-monetization stack, meaning the exposure sits with the platforms and payment/subscription rails that carry it, not just with political actors.
insights.quote: algorithmically routed into paid communities, unregulated supplements, crypto schemes, and high-ticket ‘coaching’ programs
insights.locator: In “The Grift Economy: How Young Men Are Being Sold Fake Belonging

insights.claim: The report's central framing is that masculinity itself now functions as a commercial product category that is constructed, curated and financially incentivized by online platforms.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: If identity is the category, the addressable market is demographic rather than topical — the same funnel can be re-skinned across fitness, dating, finance and supplements indefinitely.
insights.quote: ‘Masculinity’ has become a commercial category that is constructed, curated, and financially incentivized online
insights.locator: write the authors of the 153-page report

insights.claim: The monetization pipeline runs in three stages: young men arrive seeking dating, fitness or finance advice; bad actors reframe their frustrations through a grievance narrative with named enemies; then the same operators sell the 'solution' as a class, exclusive club membership or gray-market pills.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: A repeatable acquisition-to-conversion funnel is the tell of a durable revenue business, not a fad — expect it to survive individual influencer takedowns.
insights.locator: First, men encounter aspirational self-help content

insights.claim: The report documents a verified 'business' account on X using real economic data to falsely claim that high youth unemployment affects only men, illustrating how genuine labor-market data gets weaponized into targeted resentment against women, immigrants and foreign workers.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Verified-account status is being used as a credibility laundering layer for economic disinformation — a live moderation and advertiser-safety liability for X.
insights.quote: this operation converts genuine economic anxiety—which is real and documented—into resentment with named targets: women, immigrants, foreign workers.
insights.locator: By framing credential competition and labor market dynamics

themes.theme: Hard Revenue Numbers of Masculinity Influencers

insights.claim: Researchers estimate Andrew Tate generates roughly $184 million in annual gross revenue from his subscription-based 'Real World' education platform alone, which is priced at $99 per month.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: A single-operator, $184M-a-year subscription business built on course content shows creator-education economics rivaling mid-cap SaaS — and explains why the category attracts imitators faster than enforcement can remove them.
insights.locator: In breaking down the sources of the misogynist influencer Andrew Tate’s income

insights.claim: Reset Tech and Equimundo characterize manosphere membership and course products as 'fraud at scale', identifying recycled content, affiliate pyramids, deliberate cancellation barriers and deceptive testimonials as defining features of the industry's flagship products.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Deliberate cancellation barriers and deceptive testimonials are textbook FTC dark-pattern and endorsement-rule triggers — a concrete regulatory attack surface for the whole category.
insights.quote: Recycled content, affiliate pyramids, deliberate cancellation barriers, and deceptive testimonials characterize the industry’s flagship products.
insights.locator: Reset Tech and Equimundo call these kinds of membership

insights.claim: Top-tier streamers such as Adin Ross are pegged at roughly $30,000 to $50,000 in hourly streaming revenue, and Ross additionally holds an equity stake in Kick, the platform hosting his live content.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Talent holding equity in the distribution platform aligns the platform's moderation incentives with the creator's outrage output — a structural conflict worth pricing into any Kick-adjacent exposure.
insights.locator: the report pegs the range of hourly streaming revenue

insights.claim: Joe Rogan commands speaking fees upwards of $200,000, and top creators in the masculinity-content space are estimated to earn $1 million to $10 million annually across platform payouts, sponsorships, courses, memberships and speaking fees.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Diversified five-stream income means deplatforming from any single channel barely dents the economics — enforcement at one platform is not a business-model risk.
insights.quote: platform payouts, sponsorships, courses, memberships, and speaking fees
insights.locator: Figures like Joe Rogan command speaking fees

insights.claim: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate are fighting extradition to the UK on rape and sex trafficking charges after being arrested in Florida, while their revenue-generating subscription platform continues to be cited as an active business.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Criminal proceedings against the category's largest operator are the most likely near-term catalyst for payment processors and platforms to reprice manosphere-adjacent risk.
insights.locator: Tate and his brother, Tristan Tate, are fighting extradition

themes.theme: Recommendation Architecture as the Real Distributor

insights.claim: A cross-platform analysis of 216 looksmaxxing influencers on TikTok, Instagram and Facebook found combined reach exceeding 14.6 billion views during the analysis period, which the researchers attribute to recommendation architecture rather than organic demand.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: 14.6 billion algorithmically delivered views ties the harm directly to ranking systems, undercutting the 'we only host it' defense that platforms rely on in litigation and regulatory hearings.
insights.quote: The reach is not organic—it is a product of recommendation architecture.
insights.locator: Across 216 influencers tracked on TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook

insights.claim: Platforms take a cut of manosphere revenue and actively reward masculinity influencers for pushing extreme views that generate controversy and conflict, making the platforms economic participants rather than neutral hosts.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Revenue-sharing on outrage content is the mechanism regulators will target; watch for disclosure demands on payout formulas the way ad-transparency rules evolved.
insights.locator: The platforms, of course, take a cut of the profits

insights.claim: Platforms were eventually pressured into enforcement against pro-eating-disorder content targeting women but have not pursued equivalent action against content reinforcing negative body image in men to sell unhealthy behaviors, an asymmetry the report treats as unjustified.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Precedent already exists for how this gets enforced, so the gap is a policy choice — that makes it the most likely place for the next wave of platform-safety regulation to land.
insights.locator: The report draws a parallel between this harmful material

themes.theme: Outrage as Customer Acquisition: The Clavicular Case

insights.claim: Kick streamer Braden Peters, known as Clavicular, saw his X post average jump from roughly 500,000 views two weeks before a January 2026 livestream to nearly 3 million views two weeks after it, following a broadcast in which he and others listened to Kanye West's antisemitic song 'Heil Hitler' in a sprinter van in Miami.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: A ~6x engagement lift from a scandal quantifies outrage as a customer-acquisition channel with measurable ROI, which is why condemnation cycles reliably fail as a deterrent.
insights.locator: Two weeks later, he was averaging close to 3 million views

insights.claim: Clavicular's post-scandal audience spike converted directly into sales funnel for his 'looksmaxxing' academy, priced from $49 at the lowest tier up to $3,000 for private coaching.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: The tiered $49-to-$3,000 ladder shows a standard high-ticket upsell structure; attention shocks are the top-of-funnel input, so scandal frequency is a leading indicator of category revenue.
insights.locator: The larger viewership meant more potential students

insights.claim: Established figures like the Tate brothers saw little audience change from the same antisemitic livestream while the less prominent Clavicular's engagement exploded, suggesting scandal amplification pays off disproportionately for rising rather than saturated creators.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Predicts a steady supply of new, more extreme entrants competing for breakout moments — the extremity ratchet is an economic gradient, not a cultural accident.
insights.locator: While the better-known Tates saw little change in their audience

insights.claim: Equimundo founder and CEO Gary Barker argues that 18- to 29-year-old men represent the biggest traffic to these paid grievance communities yet fall outside child-protection frameworks, parental gatekeeping and legislative safeguards.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Age-verification and minor-safety regulation, the current policy default, structurally misses the highest-value segment of this market — so compliance spending won't shrink the revenue base.
insights.quote: If we're looking at the 18- to 29-year-olds, which is where we see the biggest traffic to these spaces, nobody's got their back
insights.locator: Barker says that while younger kids can be kept out

insights.claim: Reset Tech's post-2024 focus groups found young men showed a 'striking lack of self-awareness' about their information diet, treating podcasts like The Joe Rogan Experience as essentially unbiased while believing women were the ones trapped in echo chambers.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Perceived neutrality is the moat: audiences that don't recognize a channel as persuasive are cheaper to convert, which is why podcast ad rates in this segment command a premium.
insights.quote: believed women were trapped in echo chambers looking at makeup and lifestyle content while they themselves received information from neutral, verified sources
insights.locator: However, in post-2024 focus groups, Reset Tech found

insights.claim: Barker frames the audience as defrauded consumers rather than ideologues, saying they are being duped and deserve straight information on products that actually do what they claim.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Recasting the problem as consumer fraud rather than speech opens remedies — advertising standards, supplement regulation, refund enforcement — that content moderation debates cannot reach.
insights.locator: Gary Barker, founder and CEO of Equimundo

insights.claim: Absent platform action, Barker expects change to depend on users themselves exiting these communities and on the emergence of young male commentators who build audiences by exposing the grievance economy's scams — an outcome he explicitly says is not imminent.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: The only remedy on offer is slow, voluntary and unfunded, implying the multibillion-dollar revenue base persists for years absent regulatory or payment-rail intervention.
insights.quote: I think it's not gonna be a tomorrow thing
insights.locator: In the absence of action from the platforms

insights.claim: The male youth vote broke for Trump in the 2024 election following a GOP campaign built on appeals to machismo, but Gen Z men's support for the president is now plummeting during his second term without the underlying anger abating.
insights.speaker: Miles Klee
insights.so_what: Decoupling of partisan loyalty from persistent male grievance implies the commercial funnel — not party affiliation — is the durable asset, and it will monetize regardless of who holds office.
insights.locator: The male youth vote broke for Trump in the 2024 election
